label: August 31–September 06
title: “Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord” —  Psalm

items.text: The book of Psalms, known in Hebrew as _Tehillim_ meaning 'praises,' invites us to acknowledge the Lord’s power, mercy, and great deeds. While we can never repay Him, we can offer praise through singing, prayer, or testimony, leading to a deeper commitment to follow His teachings.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Psalm 102 describes feelings of anxiety and isolation, but also offers confidence to call upon the Lord in trials. As you read Psalms 102, 103, and 116, look for phrases that give you hope in Him during difficult times and mark those that inspire you.

The Psalms contain prophecies pointing to Jesus Christ's life and ministry. For instance, Psalm 110:1–4 and Psalm 118:22, 25–26 are fulfilled in Him, teaching us about His divine role and importance in our lives. Knowing this helps us understand His eternal significance.

Psalm 119 compares our lives to a journey back to Heavenly Father, using imagery of paths and ways. This psalm teaches us that God has provided His word as a guide to help us stay on His path, offering direction and light for our travels.

President Russell M. Nelson taught, 'If our journey through life is to be successful, we need to follow divine direction.' He encourages us to 'Look unto me in every thought; doubt not, fear not,' as the scriptures provide essential guidance.

The Psalmist declared, 'Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.' Scriptural guidance helps us recognize error, make corrections, and stay on the right direction. Studying this scriptural road map is crucial for our journey back home.

The Lord can comfort us in our suffering. Even when we feel anxiety and isolation, we can find confidence in calling upon His name. He offers relief and hope, guiding us through our trials with His everlasting love and mercy.

Jesus Christ fulfilled prophecies found within the Psalms. His ministry and divine role are foretold in passages like Psalm 110 and Psalm 118. Understanding these prophetic connections deepens our faith in Him and His eternal mission for mankind.

God’s word acts as a vital guide for our lives, illuminating the path back to Him. By studying scripture, we learn to navigate life's journey, recognize wrong turns, and make necessary corrections, ensuring we remain on the strait and narrow way.

The Psalms are filled with invitations to 'praise ye the Lord.' This praise can take many forms, inspiring worship and a deeper commitment to God. Whatever praise means in your life, find inspiration in the Psalms to offer your devotion.
